sourceRecord.officialPublisher: COURT_OF_APPEALS_OF_INDIANA
sourceRecord.fragment: Opinion 25A-CR-1689 states: “marijuana possession remains illegal in Indiana. See Ind. Code § 35-48-4-11 (outlawing the possession of marijuana).”

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: IOWA_DEPARTMENT_OF_HEALTH_AND_HUMAN_SERVICES
sourceRecord.fragment: Iowa HHS states that medical cannabis is currently available at five dispensaries across Iowa and lists the five locations.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Montana Legislature
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Direct Montana Code Annotated or Montana Department of Revenue material applicable only to the U.S. state of Montana.
sourceRecord.fragment: "the following acts are lawful and may not be an offense under state law ... or be a basis to impose a civil fine, penalty, or sanction, or be a basis to detain, search, or arrest" for a person 21+; including "possessing, purchasing, obtaining, using, ingesting, inhaling, or transporting 1 ounce or less of usable marijuana."

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
sourceRecord.fragment: The Therapeutic Cannabis Program maintains a confidential registry of qualifying patients, caregivers, and certifying medical providers; processes applications and issues cannabis registry ID cards to eligible patients and caregivers. Registry ID cards allow cardholders to purchase therapeutic cannabis from one of the state's licensed Alternative Treatment Centers. ATCs are independently operated entities responsible for cultivation, production, and dispensing to qualifying patients in New Hampshire.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: North Dakota Health and Human Services
sourceRecord.fragment: The current HHS patient page provides Sign In or Create an Account and states: an individual with a North Dakota medical marijuana card is only authorized to purchase and possess medical marijuana from one of the eight registered dispensaries in the state.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: State of Texas / Texas.gov
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Official State of Texas service portal explaining the Texas Compassionate Use Program administered by DPS.
sourceRecord.fragment: Eligible Texans have access to medical marijuana through the State Compassionate Use Program. A qualifying permanent Texas resident may receive a low-THC cannabis prescription from a CUP-registered physician; the physician enters it in CURT, after which the patient or legal guardian can go to any licensed dispensary to get the prescription.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Rhode Island Cannabis Control Commission
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Direct Rhode Island Cannabis Control Commission bulletin.
sourceRecord.fragment: Concentrates manufactured on or after 1 April 2026 may be offered for sale to a patient, authorized purchaser, caregiver or adult-use consumer by a licensed compassion center, hybrid retailer or adult-use retailer; the bulletin issues under R.I. Gen. Laws §21-28.11 et seq. and current Commission regulations.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: South Dakota Legislature / Legislative Research Council
sourceRecord.fragment: The current official chapter is titled CHAPTER 34-20G MEDICAL CANNABIS. Its table of contents identifies 34-20G-2 cardholder protections from arrest/prosecution/penalty, 34-20G-4 presumption for qualifying patient or designated caregiver with registry card, 34-20G-5 practitioner protections for certifications, 34-20G-14 possession of or application for registry identification card not grounds for search, and 34-20G-15 activity conducted in accordance with the chapter as lawful.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Official public authority
sourceRecord.fragment: The EOF guidance states that final medicinal-cannabis products are for direct availability to pharmacies, pharmaceutical warehouses, treatment facilities, private clinics and public hospitals under EOF control, exclusively for medical purposes; it identifies current domestic circulation rules including Decision D3(g) 40642/2024.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Saudi Food and Drug Authority official drugs-schedule publisher
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Official SFDA attached-schedules PDF for the Saudi narcotics and psychotropic-substances law; no foreign, parent or claimant regime is used.
sourceRecord.fragment: Current official bilingual schedule row 26: Cannabis and cannabis resin and Indian hemp and resin of Indian hemp; extracts and tinctures of cannabis.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: FALKLAND_ISLANDS_GOVERNMENT_LEGISLATION_PORTAL
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Official Falkland Islands legislation portal rendered PDF edition.
sourceRecord.fragment: Official rendered Ordinance schedule lists cannabis and cannabis resin as Class B controlled drugs.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Government of Gibraltar / Gibraltar Law Offices
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Direct Gibraltar source applies to Gibraltar.
sourceRecord.fragment: Sections 506(1)-(2) make possession of a controlled drug unlawful and an offence; section 508(1)-(2) make cultivation of the genus cannabis unlawful and an offence; Schedule 5 Part II Class B lists Cannabis and cannabis resin.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Government of Antigua and Barbuda - Government Printing Office / Laws portal
sourceRecord.fragment: Section 6A: “a person who is in possession of a maximum of 15 grams of the drug Cannabis or Cannabis resin is not guilty of an offence”; section 8(1A): it “shall be lawful” for the responsible household person to cultivate not more than four cannabis plants per household on the property.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Afkondigingsblad van Aruba / Minister van Toerisme, Volksgezondheid en Sport
sourceRecord.fragment: Article 1 designates cannabidiol and preparations containing cannabidiol, whether or not together with THC, as medicine. Article 2 permits a cannabidiol product containing at most 0.2% delta-9 THC to be stocked and dispensed by persons outside the usual Article 3(1) restriction.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Fiji Ministry of Health and Medical Services
sourceRecord.fragment: Section 11(1)(c): "any person may possess such quantities of an illicit drug that have been lawfully prescribed or provided for the purpose of treating a medical condition". Section 11(1)(b) exempts a lawful occupation/profession involving possession, supply or administration for that lawful purpose. Section 11(2) permits the Minister for Health, consulting the Pharmacy and Poisons Board, to license lawful import, export or manufacture of an illicit drug. Cannabis is an illicit drug under Schedule 1; unauthorised conduct remains an offence under sections 4-5.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Guam Compiler of Laws
sourceRecord.fragment: Section 8103 provides that adults 21+ may possess, use, display, purchase or transport up to one ounce of cannabis, eight grams of concentrate or 800 mg THC infused products; these acts are lawful and are not a criminal or civil offence. It also allows up to six plants, of which no more than three are mature flowering plants, subject to enclosed/private conditions.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Badan Narkotika Nasional Republik Indonesia (BNN)
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: National legislation and national regulator material of the Republic of Indonesia applies to Indonesia (ID); no dependency, claimant, country/state or alias bridge used.
sourceRecord.fragment: The 2 January 2026 circular on handling narcotics offences during transition to the new KUHP/KUHAP expressly lists Law No. 35 of 2009 as a reference.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: IDAHO_LEGISLATURE_OFFICIAL_STATUTES
sourceRecord.fragment: Current Title 37 Chapter 27 lists marijuana in Schedule I and criminalizes marijuana possession; section 37-2701 also expressly excludes FDA-approved finished-dose cannabis-derived cannabidiol products with at most 0.1% residual THC and nabiximols from the statutory marijuana definition. This narrow pharmaceutical exception prevents a full-negative cannabis conclusion.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Morocco ANRAC
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Official ANRAC implementation guide for Morocco; no extension or foreign applicability inference.
sourceRecord.fragment: Section 6.1.7, page 27: ANRAC authorizes commercialisation of transformed, manufactured, and imported cannabis/products for medical, pharmaceutical, or industrial purposes; commercialisation of medicines containing cannabis components remains subject to Law No. 17-04, the Code of Medicine and Pharmacy, and the 1922 substances regime.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: The Bahamas official legislation and health authority
sourceRecord.fragment: Under section 1(2), Monday 2 September 2024 is appointed only for Parts I, II and sections 76, 77, 78 and 82. Part V, including sections 39-48 for patient prescription and pharmacist dispensing, is not among the commenced provisions.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Arizona state authority
sourceRecord.fragment: A.R.S. § 36-2852(A): for an individual at least twenty-one, listed possession, consuming, purchasing, transport, personal home cultivation and non-remunerated transfer acts are lawful, are not an offense, and cannot ground detention, arrest or penalties; subsection (A)(1) permits one ounce or less and (A)(2) up to six plants at the primary residence subject to conditions.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: NEVADA_LEGISLATIVE_COUNSEL_BUREAU
sourceRecord.fragment: NRS 678D.200 exempts persons 21+ from state prosecution for possession, delivery or production of cannabis within specified limits and conditions, and exempts licensed adult-use cannabis establishments when acting within Title 56 and Board regulations.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Slov-Lex / Collection of Laws of the Slovak Republic
sourceRecord.fragment: §3 distinguishes Group I substances not contained as a medicine from Groups II and III contained as a medicine. §4(3) confines Group I cultivation, manufacture, import, export, dispensing, transit and wholesale distribution to research, teaching and expert activity, except industrial hemp. Schedule I expressly lists Cannabis plants, dry extract, tincture and resin except defined seed/industrial varieties.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: ATTORNEY_GENERAL_OF_SAMOA
sourceRecord.fragment: Section 2 defines cannabis plant as a prohibited plant. Section 6 penalises unlawful cultivation; section 7 prohibits possession, obtaining, consuming, smoking, use, supply or dealing unless expressly exempt, including when supplied by a licensee or pursuant to a prescription of a licensee authorised to supply or prescribe narcotics. The Second Schedule classifies cannabis, cannabis preparations, cannabis resin, cannabis oil and tetrahydrocannabinols as Class B narcotics.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Eurasian Economic Commission official repository publishing the Belarus republican controlled-substances list
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Official repository copy of the Belarus republican controlled-substances list for direct Belarus national applicability.
sourceRecord.fragment: Page 62: "Список 5 опасных наркотических средств, не используемых в медицинских целях" lists 5.1 "Гашиш", 5.4 "Марихуана", and 5.5 "Масло каннабиса (гашишное масло)".

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Saudi Food and Drug Authority official drugs-regulation publisher
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Official SFDA English implementing-procedures PDF for the Saudi Law of Combating Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances; no foreign, parent or claimant regime is used.
sourceRecord.fragment: Article 34: Narcotic drug and psychotropic substances referred to in Article (47) of the Law of Combating Narcotics Drug and Psychotropic Substances include Cannabis and Cannabis resin at 100 mg and Dronabinol at 0.5 g. Article 35: Unauthorized person should not possess narcotics or psychotropic substances unless prescribed by a licensed doctor in accordance with provisions of regulations; products obtained for treatment purpose must be returned when no longer used, and to the dispenser pharmacy if the patient died. Article 41: personal-use purpose conduct within Article 37 is punishable by a minimum of six months and not more than two years, except use in other circumstances licensed by a law.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: ILLINOIS_CANNABIS_REGULATION_OVERSIGHT_OFFICER
sourceRecord.fragment: CROO states that more than 100 dispensaries are licensed to sell cannabis to adults 21 and older and that adults 21 and older with valid identification can purchase cannabis at any Illinois dispensary.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Western Australia Parliamentary Counsel’s Office
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Cocos (Keeling) Islands Act 1955 section 8A(1) applies Western Australian laws in CC, subject only to identified inconsistent Commonwealth law or Territory Ordinance.
sourceRecord.fragment: Section 6(1)-(2) makes unauthorised prohibited-drug supply/possession/use offences; section 6(3)-(5) preserves possession, supply and use authorised under the Act or Medicines and Poisons Act 2014. Schedule I item 5 lists Cannabis, cannabis resin and any other cannabis derivative; Schedule II item 3 lists Cannabis.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, Commission on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice Legal Library
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: The document is the text of Nigeria’s Indian Hemp Act and identifies cannabis, cannabis resin and preparations in its operative definitions. The hosting authority is UNODC, not a Nigerian domestic consolidated-legislation portal.
sourceRecord.fragment: Sections 1-5 and 7, printed pages I6-2 and I6-3.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Authority Sanitaria of the Republic of San Marino
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Official Authority Sanitaria publication for the Republic of San Marino; no parent, claimant or foreign regime is used.
sourceRecord.fragment: All’Authority Sanitaria è attribuita la funzione di ASCC, i cui compiti sono quelli di: a) autorizzare le richieste di coltivazione, trasformazione e commercio di cannabis; b) autorizzare l’importazione, l’esportazione, la distribuzione all’ingrosso di cannabis e prodotti a base di cannabis.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Montana Department of Revenue, Cannabis & Alcohol Regulation
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Direct Montana Code Annotated or Montana Department of Revenue material applicable only to the U.S. state of Montana.
sourceRecord.fragment: "Adult-use dispensaries may sell to registered cardholders, adults over 21 years of age, or both." "Licensed Dispensary Locations — August 2026"; current listed rows are marked "Adult Use".

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Ålands landskapsregering / Åland Government
sourceRecord.fragment: The 16 May 2025 protocol states that Fimea requested an opinion on an Åland pharmacy service-point licence; under Autonomy Act section 27(30), the pharmacy system belongs to the realm legislative competence, and the Åland Government recommends the licence under Medicines Act (FFS 395/1987) section 52a(1).

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Government of Antigua and Barbuda - Government Printing Office / Laws portal
sourceRecord.fragment: Sections 45-48 require Authority-registered and Minister-approved medical professionals, allow numbered recommendations for qualifying patients, and authorise a patient with a recommendation and identification card to obtain, possess, store and use medicinal cannabis; the card may be issued by an authorised dispensary and ultimately the Authority.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Parliament of The Bahamas, Extraordinary Official Gazette
sourceRecord.fragment: Arrangement of Sections: Part V - Access to Cannabis, sections 36-48; sections 39-48 cover medical practitioner prescription, electronic prescription, and pharmacist dispensing. Section 1(2) permits different dates for different Parts or sections by Gazette notice.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Medicines Control Authority of Zimbabwe (MCAZ)
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Zimbabwe national legislation or MCAZ national regulatory authority; direct territorial applicability.
sourceRecord.fragment: Section 3 applies Part II to "cannabis plant"; section 6 authorises regulation to "prohibit, control or restrict the production, possession, sale, use or distribution" of covered drugs and makes contravention an offence.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Medicines Control Authority of Zimbabwe (MCAZ)
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Zimbabwe national legislation or MCAZ national regulatory authority; direct territorial applicability.
sourceRecord.fragment: Title: "Dangerous Drugs (Production of Cannabis for Medicinal and Scientific Use) Regulations, 2018"; arrangement includes producers licences, import/export, persons authorised to handle cannabis and research and development.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Government of Antigua and Barbuda - Government Printing Office / Laws portal
sourceRecord.fragment: Section 6B is replaced “Notwithstanding section 6A” to punish smoking cannabis in a public place, or knowingly permitting sale, supply or smoking there, with a summary fine not exceeding $2,000. The Act repeals section 13A, not section 6A.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Republic of Albania National Agency for Cannabis Control; Assembly of the Republic of Albania
sourceRecord.fragment: Article 5(1)(d)-(e): Albania prohibits use of cannabis plant by-products/final products except as provided by law and applicable legislation, and prohibits retail or wholesale sale, distribution, acquisition, or consumption of cannabis by-products/final products for medical purposes in Albania.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Inspectie Volksgezondheid Aruba, Central Wettenregister
sourceRecord.fragment: Article 4(1) prohibits import/export, cultivation, preparation, sale, delivery, possession and use of hemp/cannabis and cannabis resin/hashish; Article 6(1) creates a ministerial-consent exception for Article 4(1)(A); Article 7(1)-(3) creates written-permit and medicinal professional/own-medical-use exceptions; Article 11 sets penalties.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: French Interministerial Mission for Combating Drugs and Addictive Behaviours
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: French DILA Guide 3.6.1 identifies Mayotte as an Article 73 collectivity under legislative identity: French laws and regulations apply there by right; no separate territorial cannabis statute is inferred.
sourceRecord.fragment: Narcotic classification prohibits free use, production, manufacture, import, export, transport, possession, offering and sale.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Qendra e Botimeve Zyrtare (Official Publications Centre), Republic of Albania
sourceRecord.fragment: Article 283 criminalises listed narcotics conduct and possession except for personal use and small doses; the page visibly records Law No. 8 of 28 January 2026 amendments. Article 284 criminalises cultivation of plants used for narcotic/psychotropic substances without statutory permit and authorisation.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Afkondigingsblad van Aruba / Minister van Toerisme, Volksgezondheid en Sport
sourceRecord.fragment: Article 1 provides that hemp preparations, extracts and tinctures are narcotics except cannabidiol or cannabidiol preparations, extracts or tinctures with delta-9 THC at most 0.2%. Article 2 provides entry into force on the day after publication.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Minnesota Legislature / Office of the Revisor of Statutes
sourceRecord.fragment: Section 11 amends only section 342.09, subdivision 3, Home extraction of cannabis concentrate by use of volatile solvent prohibited, and states: “This section is effective January 1, 2027.”

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Minnesota Legislature / Office of the Revisor of Statutes
sourceRecord.fragment: Subdivision 1: an individual at least 21 years of age may use, possess, or transport cannabis flower and cannabinoid products, including up to two ounces in public and two pounds at a private residence. Subdivision 2: up to eight plants, no more than four mature flowering plants, may be grown at an eligible single residence by an individual 21 or older without a cultivation license.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Oregon Legislative Assembly
sourceRecord.fragment: Official Chapter 475C compilation contains the Oregon Medical Marijuana Act and adult-use possession provisions, including §475C.337.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Direct Washington State Legislature statute or Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board regulator page applicable to Washington State only.
sourceRecord.fragment: LCB states that adult non-medical cannabis became legal in Washington in 2012, retail stores opened in 2014, only adults 21+ may possess or use adult-use cannabis, and cannabis products must be bought from a state-licensed retail store.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department / Cannabis Control Division
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department publishes the New Mexico state cannabis statute compilation; Article 2C applies within New Mexico only.
sourceRecord.fragment: Section 26-2C-25(A): for a person 21 or older, listed conduct is lawful; it includes possessing, using, purchasing, obtaining and transporting cannabis, transferring without financial consideration to another person 21 or older, consuming cannabis lawfully purchased, and limited home planting/cultivation/harvesting/manufacture. Section 26-2C-26 provides limits and civil penalties rather than negating the lawful conduct.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Greenland Self-Government
sourceRecord.fragment: Annex 1 identifies List B and lists Cannabis as item 59, defined as all above-ground parts of plants belonging to the Cannabis genus from which resin has not been removed, excluding hemp seeds and isolated hemp fibre.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Rechtsdienst der Regierung, Principality of Liechtenstein
sourceRecord.legalBasisForExtension: Official Liechtenstein legal database or Liechtenstein state annual report; direct domestic applicability.
sourceRecord.fragment: Art. 6(1)(d): narcotics of the cannabis effect type with an average total THC content of at least 1 percent may not be cultivated, manufactured or placed on the market.

sourceRecord.officialPublisher: Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Niger
sourceRecord.fragment: Article 2 defines Table I as high-risk plants, substances and preparations devoid of medical interest. Article 8 prohibits cultivation of the cannabis plant nationally. Article 9 prohibits production, manufacture, wholesale/retail commerce, transport, possession, offer, transfer, acquisition, use, import, export and transit for Table I. Article 10’s human/veterinary-medicine framework applies to Tables II and III. Annex Table I lists “Cannabis et résine de cannabis.”
